svg.title: Figure 6 — Expansion, admission, budget check, eviction and the report
svg.desc: A vertical flow from a user expanding a node to the toast that reports what happened. The steps are: the gesture, expandNode, neighboursOf, the wanted and slice lists, addToView, the budget check, the three overflow modes, node creation, edge linking, the simulation wake-up, the returned report, the toast, and the budget meter update.
svg.text: FIGURE 6
Expansion to eviction to report — the whole admission path
Nothing enters the viewport except through addToView(), and addToView() never exceeds the budget. The user is always told what it cost.
User gesture
dblclick a node · context menu Expand · Enter on the selection
Four entry points, one path. “Expand 20 only” passes limit = 20;
every other gesture leaves limit undefined, which means the budget.
Reveal in graph and Send page to graph enter at step 5 instead.
expandNode(u, limit)
const n = G.nodes.get(u); if (!n) return null;
Precondition: the node must already be in the viewport. Expanding
something that is not shown is not an expansion, it is a seed.
neighboursOf(u) → { list, total }
list capped at NEIGHBOUR_CAP = 4000 · total is the honest degree
The cap is on the returned list, not on the count. total feeds the
node radius and the hidden-neighbour badge, so a class with 100,000
instances still reports 100,000 while costing one bucket read.
Candidate list
wanted = list not already in view · slice = wanted.slice(0, cap)
cap = limit ?? G.budget. Neighbours already on screen are dropped
here, before the budget is ever consulted — re-expanding a node that
is fully shown costs nothing and evicts nothing.
addToView(slice, { dist: n.dist + 1, seed: n })
already-present IRIs: touched = ++G.clock, dist = min(dist, existing)
Touching an existing node refreshes its LRU clock and can only lower
its graph distance, never raise it. That is what stops a node drifting
outward in the eviction order just because it was reached again.
fresh.length ≤ room ?
room = G.budget − G.nodes.size
yes — admit all
no — over budget
ON OVERFLOW — G.evictMode, set from the budget panel
refuse
refused = fresh.length − max(0, room); the list is truncated. Nothing leaves.
degree
need = fresh.length − room; evictionOrder() sorted by distance, then
in-view degree, then touch clock. See Figure 7.
lru
the same eviction, ordered by n.touched alone — oldest touch leaves first.
If eviction cannot free enough — every remaining node is pinned or focused — the shortfall becomes refused and the slice is truncated again.
makeNode() for each admitted IRI
golden-angle seeding around the expanded node · r = nodeRadius(total, kind)
neighbourhood arrives already spread out rather than as a spike.
linkNode() for each admitted node
an edge exists only when both endpoints are in view · shownDeg++ on both
Edges are created in a second pass, after every node exists, so a
neighbourhood admitted together is linked together. hiddenNeighbours(n)
= max(0, n.deg − n.shownDeg) is what the +n badge reports.
Wake the simulation
G.alpha = Math.max(G.alpha, 0.9); G.rev++;
G.rev is part of layoutKey(), so the next stepLayout() sees a changed
key and relayouts. Alpha is raised, never reset, so a burst of
expansions does not restart the cooling schedule from scratch.
Return the report
{ added, evicted, refused, evictedNames, requested, totalDegree }
evictedNames holds at most three labels — enough to name what went,
not enough to become a wall of text. expandNode() then sets
n.expanded only when nothing was truncated and nothing was refused.
reportView(rep, label)
refused wins over evicted; a clean expansion says nothing at all
refused → “Budget reached at 1,000 nodes. 412 neighbours of Pizza
Topping were left out — raise the budget or unpin something.”
evicted → “Budget held at 1,000. Paged out 38 nodes furthest from the
focus (Cajun, Caprina, Capricciosa, …) to make room for Pizza Topping.”
updateBudgetUI() and the next frame
meter width · is-near ≥ 75% · is-full ≥ 98% · in view · hidden · zoom
The meter changes colour and the in-view and hidden-neighbour counts
are rewritten. On the next animation frame stepLayout() notices the
new layoutKey() and re-runs the chosen layout over the new node set.
Figure 6 · Expansion and eviction. Illustrates 20-graph-viewport-and-budget.md, “Admission” and “Overflow policy”. [src: expandNode(), addToView(), evictionOrder(), reportView()]
The invariant the whole path exists to protect: G.nodes.size never exceeds G.budget, whatever the user asks for, and the user is never silently given less than they asked for.
